faq.a: Umrah is an act of worship and devotion that allows believers to get closer to Allah, seek forgiveness and renew their faith. Unlike Hajj, it can be performed at any time of the year.

faq.q: Are there age restrictions for pilgrimage?
faq.a: There is no formal age restriction. Children must be accompanied by a guardian. We adapt our accompaniment to each pilgrim's profile.
Yes, the meningitis vaccine is mandatory. The yellow fever vaccine may be required depending on the country. Our team guides you through all health procedures.

faq.q: Can one perform Hajj or Umrah alone?
faq.a: It is strongly recommended to travel with an accredited agency to benefit from full supervision. For Hajj, agency supervision is mandatory in Niger.

faq.q: What are your departure dates and prices?
faq.a: Umrah August 2026 (Aug 04-23) from 1,250,000 FCFA/pers. Hajj 2027 from 3,184,500 FCFA. Check our offers page for full details.

history.heroBadge: HAJJ ET OUMRA ZAM — OUR STORY
history.heroTitle: The people behind Hajj et Oumra ZAM
history.heroSubtitle: The people who carry Hajj et Oumra ZAM, serving pilgrims since 1998 — from Niamey to the Holy Land.
history.teamSubtitle: A team united by the same calling: to accompany you to the Holy Land with faith, rigor and humanity.

team.name: El Hadj Moussa Abdou
team.bio: Born in Niamey in a family deeply attached to Islamic values, El Hadj Moussa Abdou accompanied his first pilgrims in 1998. That journey was a revelation: he saw it as a life mission. For twenty years, he patiently built a reputation for seriousness, integrity and sincere love for pilgrims.
team.bio2: Under his leadership, Hajj et Oumra ZAM obtained its official COHO accreditation in 2018 and established itself as an essential reference for pilgrims from Niger and West Africa.

team.name: Ibrahima Moussa
team.bio: Son of the founder, Ibrahima grew up in contact with pilgrims. He accompanied his father from adolescence, learning the operational rigor and human kindness that mark Hajj et Oumra ZAM.
team.bio2: With a degree in hotel management and a passion for continuous improvement, he took over as general manager of the agency in 2020 with the mission of modernizing services while preserving the founding spirit.

team.name: Fatouma Adamou
team.bio: Fatouma has made more than fifteen trips to Saudi Arabia as a supervisor. She knows the hotels, the circuits, the unexpected situations and the solutions. Her presence reassures pilgrims, especially the elderly and first-time pilgrims.
team.bio2: She supervises the design of programs, hotel selection and training of local guides — ensuring that every stay delivers on its promises.

team.name: Youssouf Hamidou
team.bio: IATA affiliated since 2019, Youssouf masters the workings of airline ticketing and group logistics. He negotiates the best Niamey – Jeddah connections and coordinates on-site transfers.
team.bio2: Methodical and principled, he ensures that no file is incomplete on the day of departure — a requirement he set for himself personally since his first Hajj.

guide.title: Pilgrim's Guide
guide.subtitle: Everything you need to know for your pilgrimage
guide.bottomDesc: Hajj & Umrah ZAM has been accompanying you for over 25 years for your Hajj and Umrah.

pilgrimages.title: Hajj Tamattu'
pilgrimages.desc: Perform Umrah then Hajj separately during the same trip. This is the most common form for foreign pilgrims.

pilgrimages.title: Hajj Ifrad
pilgrimages.desc: Perform only Hajj, without Umrah in the same trip. The state of Ihram is maintained from the Miqat until the Hajj rites.

pilgrimages.title: Hajj Qiran
pilgrimages.desc: Combine Umrah and Hajj in a single continuous Ihram. The pilgrim performs the rites of both pilgrimages without exiting the sacred state between them.

guide.introDesc: Islamic pilgrimage mainly takes two forms: Umrah (the lesser pilgrimage, performable at any time of year) and Hajj (the major pilgrimage, fifth pillar of Islam). Hajj itself can be performed in three ways:
guide.oumraSectionDesc1: Umrah is an act of worship that consists of going to Mecca to perform specific rites. Unlike Hajj, it is not obligatory but highly recommended. It can be performed at any time of year.
guide.oumraSectionDesc2: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'From one Umrah to the next is expiation for what comes between them, and an accepted Hajj has no reward except Paradise.'

oumraRituals.title: Preparation for consecration (Ihram)
oumraRituals.content: Before entering Ihram, it is recommended to purify oneself: purification bath (Ghusl), trimming nails, removing excess hair. For men, it is advised to apply perfume before donning the Ihram garments.

oumraRituals.title: Consecration garments
oumraRituals.content: For men: two pieces of unsewn white cloth — the Izar (lower piece wrapped around the waist) and the Rida (upper piece draped over the shoulders). Sandals are permitted. For women: usual covering garments, without covering the face or hands.

oumraRituals.title: Departure to Mecca — the Miqat
oumraRituals.content: The Miqat is the mandatory crossing point to enter Ihram. For pilgrims from Medina, the Miqat is Dhu al-Hulayfah. There one formulates the intention for Umrah and pronounces the Talbiyah.

oumraRituals.title: The Talbiyah
oumraRituals.content: After the intention, one pronounces: 'Labbayk Allahumma labbayk, labbayk la sharika laka labbayk, innal hamda wan ni'mata laka wal mulk, la sharika lak.' (Here I am, O Allah, here I am!)

oumraRituals.title: Prohibitions during Ihram
oumraRituals.content: For all: cutting hair or nails, using perfume, getting married, conjugal relations, hunting. Additionally for men: covering the head, wearing sewn clothes. For women: covering the face.

oumraRituals.title: Arrival in Mecca — First sight of the Ka'bah
oumraRituals.content: Upon seeing the Ka'bah for the first time, it is recommended to raise one's hands and make supplications. Some scholars advise saying: 'Allahumma zid hadhâl bayta tashrifan wa ta'dhiman wa takriman wa mahâbatan.'

oumraRituals.title: The Tawaf
oumraRituals.content: Circumambulation around the Ka'bah 7 times counterclockwise, starting and ending at the Black Stone (Hajar al-Aswad). Begin with Istilam (touching or greeting the Black Stone), then complete 7 circuits reciting supplications.

oumraRituals.title: The Sa'i between Safa and Marwa
oumraRituals.content: Seven back-and-forth walks between the hills of Safa and Marwa, commemorating the run of Hajar (Hagar), wife of Ibrahim (Abraham), in search of water for her son Ismail. Begin at Safa and end at Marwa.

oumraRituals.title: End of Umrah — Tahallul
oumraRituals.content: After Sa'i, one exits Ihram by completely shaving the head (Halq) or shortening the hair (Taqsir). Shaving is preferable for men. After this, all Ihram prohibitions are lifted.

guide.hajjSectionDesc1: Hajj is the fifth pillar of Islam. It is obligatory once in a lifetime for every adult Muslim who is of sound mind and has the physical and financial means. It takes place from the 8th to 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah.
guide.hajjSectionDesc2: Every year, millions of pilgrims from around the world converge on Mecca to perform this fundamental rite. Allah says in the Quran:
guide.hajjVerseAr: « وَلِلَّهِ عَلَى النَّاسِ حِجُّ الْبَيْتِ مَنِ اسْتَطَاعَ إِلَيْهِ سَبِيلًا »
guide.hajjVerseTr: 'And [due] to Allah from the people is a pilgrimage to the House — for whoever is able to find thereto a way.' (Surah Al-Imran, 3:97)

hajjDays.title: Yawm al-Tarwiyah — Departure to Mina
hajjDays.content: On the morning of the 8th, the pilgrim enters Ihram from their place of residence in Mecca. They then depart to Mina to spend the day and night, performing Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha and Fajr prayers (each at their proper time, shortened but not combined).

hajjDays.title: Yawm Arafah — The pillar of Hajj
hajjDays.content: This is the most important day of Hajj. After Fajr prayer, pilgrims head to Arafat. They combine and shorten Dhuhr and Asr prayers, then stand at Arafat until sunset, supplicating Allah. 'Hajj is Arafat.'

hajjDays.title: Collecting pebbles
hajjDays.content: After sunset, pilgrims head to Muzdalifah where they combine Maghrib and Isha prayers. They spend the night and collect pebbles for the stoning the next day (minimum 49 pebbles the size of a chickpea).

hajjDays.title: Yawm al-Nahr — Day of sacrifice
hajjDays.content: This day involves 4 acts in order: 1) Stoning the large Jamarat with 7 pebbles. 2) Sacrificing an animal. 3) Shaving or shortening hair (first partial desacralization). 4) Tawaf al-Ifadah and Sa'i (complete desacralization).

hajjDays.title: Days of Tashriq — Mina
hajjDays.content: Pilgrims return to Mina to spend the nights. Each day after Dhuhr, they stone the three Jamarats (small, medium, large) with 7 pebbles each. It is permitted to leave Mina after the 12th stoning before sunset (early departure).

hajjDays.title: Tawaf al-Wada' — The farewell
hajjDays.content: Before leaving Mecca, each pilgrim must perform the farewell Tawaf (7 circumambulations around the Ka'bah). This is the last act of Hajj. Women in their menstrual period are exempt.

guide.duasDesc: Essential supplications for the pilgrim, step by step — in Arabic, phonetics and translation.

duas.title: Supplication for the traveller (for the one staying behind)
duas.arabic: استودعكم الله الذي لا تضيع ودائعه
duas.translation: I entrust you to Allah, the One Whose deposits are never lost.

duas.title: Supplication upon leaving the house
duas.arabic: بسم الله، توكلت على الله، لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله
duas.phonetic: Bismillâhi, Tawakaltou Alalâhi, Lâ hawla walâ qouwwata Illâ billâhi.
duas.translation: In the name of Allah. I put my trust in Allah. There is no might and no power except with Allah.

duas.title: Supplication for travel (upon the mount)
duas.arabic: سبحان الذي سخر لنا هذا وما كنا له مقرنين
duas.phonetic: Soubhânallazî sakhara lanâ hâzâ wa mâ kounnâ lahoû mouqrinîna.
duas.translation: Glory to Him Who has subjected this to us, and we could never have it by our efforts, and to our Lord we surely must return.

duas.title: Supplication upon entering the mosque
duas.phonetic: Bismillâhi was'salâtou wassalâmou alâ rasoûlilâhi, allâhoumma iftah lî abwâba rahmatika.
duas.translation: In the name of Allah, peace and blessings be upon the Messenger of Allah. O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy.

duas.title: Supplication upon leaving the mosque
duas.phonetic: Bismillâhi, was'salâtou wassalâmou alâ rasoûlilâhi. Allâhoumma asalouka min fadlika.
duas.translation: In the name of Allah, peace and blessings be upon the Messenger of Allah. O Allah, I ask of You from Your bounty.

duas.title: What to say at the tomb of the Prophet ﷺ
duas.arabic: السلام عليك أيها النبي ورحمة الله وبركاته
duas.phonetic: Assalâmou alyka ayyouhan'nabiyyou warahamatoullâhi wa barakâtouhou.
duas.translation: Peace, mercy and blessings of Allah be upon you, O Prophet!

duas.title: Supplication when visiting the cemetery (Al-Baqi')
duas.arabic: السلام عليكم أهل الديار، من المؤمنين والمسلمين
duas.translation: Peace be upon you, O inhabitants of these dwellings, believers and Muslims.

duas.title: The Talbiyah — What to say when entering Ihram
duas.arabic: لبيك اللهم لبيك، لبيك لا شريك لك لبيك، إن الحمد والنعمة لك والملك لا شريك لك
duas.phonetic: Labbaykal-lâhoumma labbayka, Labbayka lâ charîka laka labbayka.
duas.translation: Here I am, O Allah, here I am! Here I am, You have no partner, here I am! Praise, grace and sovereignty belong to You. You have no partner.

duas.title: What to say at the beginning of Tawaf
duas.arabic: بسم الله، والله أكبر، اللهم إيمانا بك
duas.phonetic: Bismillâhi, wal-lâhou akbar, Allâhoumma îmânan bika.
duas.translation: In the name of Allah, Allah is the Greatest. O Allah, with faith in You and trust in Your Book.

duas.title: Supplication between the Yemeni corner and the Black Stone
duas.arabic: ربنا آتنا في الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة حسنة وقنا عذاب النار
duas.phonetic: Rabbanâ âtinâ fiddouniyâ hassanatan wa fil âkhirati hassanatan waqinâ azâbannâri.
duas.translation: Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.

duas.title: Supplication at the Station of Ibrahim
duas.translation: And take the Station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer. (Surah Al-Baqarah, 2:125)

duas.title: Supplication for drinking Zamzam water
duas.translation: In the name of Allah. Then make your own supplications while drinking.

duas.title: Supplication on Mount Safa (and Marwa)
duas.arabic: الله أكبر، الله أكبر، الله أكبر — لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له
duas.phonetic: Allâhou Akbar (3×), lâ ilâha illal'lâhou wahadahou lâ charîka lahou.
duas.translation: Allah is the Greatest (3×). There is no deity but Allah, Alone, without partner. To Him belongs sovereignty and all praise, and He is over all things capable.

duas.title: Supplication on the Day of Arafah
duas.arabic: لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، له الملك وله الحمد
duas.phonetic: lâ ilâha illal'lâhou wahadahou lâ charîka lahou, lahoul'moulkou wa lahoul'hamdou.
duas.translation: There is no deity but Allah, Alone, without partner. To Him belongs sovereignty and praise, and He is over all things capable.

duas.title: What to say during the stoning of the Jamarats
duas.translation: In the name of Allah, Allah is the Greatest. (To be said with each pebble thrown.)

guide.conclusionText1: Thus end the rites of Hajj. May Allah accept the pilgrimage of all the faithful and grant them His mercy. All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the Worlds.
guide.conclusionText2: Good physical, mental and spiritual preparation is essential. The Hajj & Umrah ZAM team is here to accompany you at every step and allow you to experience this sacred moment in complete serenity.
